item.painLine: I'm not heard by the people in charge.
item.title: Voting in the local elections where a few votes decide
item.line: I vote for mayor, city council and school board, not just for president, because those races are often decided by very few people.

fixes.title: Put the next local election date on your calendar
fixes.whatChanges: A Portland State University study of four cities found mayoral turnout as low as 7% of registered voters, in Charlotte’s primary. When so few people vote, each vote is a much bigger share of the result.
fixes.example: Portland State University 'Who Votes for Mayor' pilot · Portland, Charlotte, Detroit and St. Paul · 2016 · Mayoral turnout as low as 7% (Charlotte primary); registered voters 65+ about 10 times as likely to vote as those 18-34
fixes.firstStep: Look up your city’s next election date on your county elections website and add it to your calendar.

fixes.title: Ask a younger friend to vote with you
fixes.whatChanges: The same study found registered voters 65 and older were about 10 times as likely to vote in those mayoral races as voters 18 to 34. Whoever shows up is who local officials hear from, so a couple of friends who start voting changes who that is.
fixes.example: Portland State University 'Who Votes for Mayor' pilot · Portland, Charlotte, Detroit and St. Paul · 2016 · Mayoral turnout as low as 7% (Charlotte primary); registered voters 65+ about 10 times as likely to vote as those 18-34
fixes.firstStep: Text one friend who usually skips local elections and ask if they want to go vote together.

fixes.title: Search past city council meetings for your issue
fixes.whatChanges: Council Data Project, started by a University of Washington professor and a student after they followed a Seattle City Council vote on an arena, turns council meetings in 17 cities into searchable transcripts. fixes.firstStep: Search your city's meeting minutes or council transcripts for your issue and note who spoke about it.

fixes.title: Look up whether your state lawmakers have taken up the issue
fixes.whatChanges: Open States, a free tool from Plural, shows your state lawmakers from your address and keeps a record of state bills. A bill on your issue usually comes with groups that testified for or against it.
fixes.example: Open States legislator lookup and legislative data · United States · 2026 · Free lookup of your state lawmakers by location, plus bulk legislative data and an API

item.painLine: I don't sleep well.
item.title: A bedroom that stays dark and quiet all night
item.line: Streetlights, early sun and traffic noise stop waking me up.

fixes.title: Put up blackout curtains or wear an eye mask
fixes.whatChanges: A Northwestern study found that one night with a room light on raised people’s heart rate and made their bodies handle sugar worse the next morning. The researchers’ rule of thumb: if you can see things clearly in your bedroom, it’s too bright.
fixes.example: Northwestern Medicine light-during-sleep study · Chicago, IL · 2022 · One night with room light (100 lux) raised heart rate and next-morning insulin resistance vs dim light (3 lux)
fixes.firstStep: Stand in your bedroom tonight with the lights off and notice where light gets in.

fixes.title: Run a steady sound like pink or white noise
fixes.whatChanges: A smooth background sound makes sudden noises like a door or a car less jarring. A 2022 review of 34 studies found the research thin, but pink noise did better than white noise and nobody found it harmful.
fixes.example: Systematic review of white and pink noise for sleep (Capezuti et al.) · Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine · 2022 · 34 studies; 9 of 11 pink-noise studies positive, under a third of white-noise studies
fixes.firstStep: Play a free pink-noise track at low volume tonight and notice whether you wake up less.

fixes.title: Try sleep earbuds that cover up snoring and traffic
fixes.whatChanges: Earbuds made for sleep, such as Ozlo’s, seal out some sound and play quiet masking noise over the rest. They cost about $279, so foam earplugs are worth trying first.
fixes.example: Ozlo Sleepbuds noise-masking earbuds · United States · 2025 · $279; passive seal plus masking sounds, up to 14 hours a charge
fixes.firstStep: Buy a pack of foam earplugs and try them for three nights.

item.painLine: I put things off.
item.title: Understanding the feeling that makes me put things off
item.line: When I notice I’m avoiding something, I can name what it makes me feel and still take the first step.

fixes.title: Name the feeling the task brings up
fixes.whatChanges: The psychologists Sirois and Pychyl argued in 2013 that putting things off is mostly about getting away from a bad feeling right now, like boredom, worry or self-doubt, rather than a lack of willpower. Knowing which feeling you’re dodging often tells you what would make the task easier, such as company for a boring job or a second opinion for a scary one.
fixes.example: Procrastination as short-term mood repair (F. Sirois and T. Pychyl) · 2013 · Review argues procrastination is mainly about escaping bad feelings now, at the cost of the future self
fixes.firstStep: Write the task down, and next to it write the one word for how it makes you feel.

fixes.title: Forgive yourself for the last time you put it off
fixes.whatChanges: In a 2010 study of 134 first-year college students, the ones who forgave themselves for putting off studying for their first exams put off studying less before the next round. Being hard on yourself tends to make the task feel worse, and the students who went easier on themselves did better.
fixes.example: Self-forgiveness and procrastination study (Wohl, Pychyl and Bennett) · Canada · 2010 · 134 first-year students who forgave themselves for procrastinating before first exams procrastinated less before the second
fixes.firstStep: Say or write one sentence letting yourself off the hook for the last delay, then look at what’s next.

item.painLine: I don't sleep well.
item.title: Falling asleep without pills or dread
item.line: I go to bed expecting to sleep, and most nights I do.

fixes.title: Ask your doctor about short, drug-free insomnia therapy
fixes.whatChanges: In a large trial in England’s health service, four short sessions with a practice nurse helped people with insomnia more than the usual advice leaflet, without pills. This therapy isn’t right for everyone, so the nurse checks first.
fixes.example: HABIT trial: nurse-delivered sleep restriction · NHS general practices, England · 2024 · 642 adults; four short nurse sessions cut insomnia scores by 3 points vs leaflet
fixes.firstStep: Write down when you went to bed and got up for the next week, so you have something to bring.

fixes.title: Try an online insomnia course your doctor recommends
fixes.whatChanges: England’s health guidance body recommended an online course called Sleepio over sleeping pills in 2022, after reviewing 12 trials. You do the course on your phone or computer, in your own time.
fixes.example: NICE guidance on Sleepio digital CBT-I · England · 2022 · Recommended over sleeping pills after 12 randomised trials
fixes.firstStep: Ask your doctor at your next visit whether there’s an online insomnia course they’d recommend.

fixes.title: Keep a simple morning sleep diary
fixes.whatChanges: Sleep experts agreed on a standard nine-question morning diary in 2012, and it’s what therapists ask for first. It could ask you those questions each morning and turn the answers into a summary you can show a doctor.
fixes.example: Consensus Sleep Diary (Carney et al.) · Sleep journal · 2012 · A standard 9-question morning diary built by 25 insomnia experts
fixes.firstStep: Tell us you’d use this, and tomorrow morning jot down when you went to bed and when you woke up.

item.painLine: I'm not heard by the people in charge.
item.title: Randomly chosen residents advising on hard questions
item.line: When my state faces a hard question, a group of ordinary residents drawn by lot studies it, and lawmakers have to answer what they recommend.

fixes.title: Learn how a randomly chosen citizens’ assembly works
fixes.whatChanges: In 2016 Ireland drew 99 citizens at random, matched to the census by age, gender, class and region, to study the abortion amendment in its constitution. Most of them, 64%, recommended a change, and in the 2018 referendum 66.4% of voters agreed. People still disagree strongly about the outcome; what drew attention elsewhere was the process.
fixes.example: Irish Citizens' Assembly · Ireland · 2016 · 99 randomly chosen members; 64% backed changing the abortion amendment; the 2018 referendum passed with 66.4%
fixes.firstStep: Read a one-page summary of the Irish assembly and write down one question you’d want such a group in your state to take on.

fixes.title: Ask lawmakers for a permanent citizens’ panel
fixes.whatChanges: Since 2019 the German-speaking region of Belgium has had a 24-person citizens’ council, drawn by lot, that picks topics for citizens’ panels. Their advice isn’t binding, but parliament must debate it twice within a year.
fixes.example: Ostbelgien permanent Citizens' Council · German-speaking Community of Belgium · 2019 · A 24-person council drawn by lot sets topics for citizens' panels; parliament must debate their recommendations twice within a year
fixes.firstStep: Write your state legislator a short note asking whether they’d support a trial citizens’ panel on one local issue.

fixes.title: Ask what lawmakers must do with the panel’s advice
fixes.whatChanges: France’s citizens’ convention on climate made 149 recommendations in 2020. The president rejected 3 outright and the climate bill fully included 46, which left many participants disappointed. A panel works best when everyone knows ahead of time what the government owes it.
fixes.example: French Citizens' Convention for Climate · France · 2020 · 149 recommendations; 3 rejected outright, 46 fully included in the climate bill, others partly included or weakened
fixes.firstStep: In your note, ask what the legislature would be required to do with the panel’s recommendations.

item.painLine: I put things off.
item.title: Getting boring tasks done with someone else there
item.line: I sit down with a friend, or on a video call with a stranger, and we both get through the tasks we’ve been avoiding.

fixes.title: Do your task while a friend does theirs
fixes.whatChanges: Having another person nearby, even one doing something completely different, can make it easier to stay with a dull or uncomfortable task. An ADHD coach named this body doubling, and people without ADHD use it too.
fixes.example: Focusmate article on body doubling · 1996 · Body doubling means working with another person present, in person or virtually, while they do something unrelated; term coined by ADHD coach Linda Anderson in 1996; reported benefits strongest among people with ADHD but not limited to them
fixes.firstStep: Text a friend and ask if they’d like to spend an hour this week working on your own lists side by side.

fixes.title: Book a video work session with a stranger
fixes.whatChanges: Focusmate pairs you on video with another person for 25, 50 or 75 minutes: you each say what you’ll work on, work quietly, and check in at the end. Three sessions a week are free.
fixes.example: Focusmate virtual body doubling · Online · Paired 25-, 50- or 75-minute video work sessions; three free sessions a week
fixes.firstStep: Book one 25-minute session for the task you’ve been putting off longest.

fixes.title: Put money on a deadline with a friend as referee
fixes.whatChanges: On stickK, a site started in 2008 by two Yale economists, you set a goal, pick a friend to confirm whether you did it, and put money on it that goes elsewhere if you miss. The co-founder reported that 78% of people who used both money and a referee reached their goal, compared with 35% of those who put no money down.
fixes.example: stickK commitment contracts · New Haven, CT · 2008 · Co-founder reported 78% of users with money and a referee reached goals, versus 35% with no money down
fixes.firstStep: Choose one task, a date, and a friend you’d trust to say honestly whether you did it.

item.painLine: I see the gap between those with plenty and those struggling grow.
item.title: Owning a share of the company I work for
item.line: When the business I work for does well, I get part of the gain, not just my wages.

fixes.title: Ask your boss what happens to the business when they retire
fixes.whatChanges: Project Equity, a nonprofit in Oakland, estimates that baby boomers own 2.34 million American businesses employing 24.7 million people, and one estimate says about 80 percent of those businesses have no plan for what happens next. Selling to the employees is one way to keep the jobs, and the owner still gets paid for the business.
fixes.example: Project Equity estimate of baby boomer–owned businesses · United States · 2017 · Project Equity, an Oakland, California-based nonprofit, says baby boomers own 2.34 million businesses employing 24.7 million people; a separate estimate says 80 percent of these businesses lack a plan for what comes next
fixes.firstStep: Ask your boss, casually, whether they've thought about who takes over when they step back.

fixes.title: Share how one founder handed most of his company to staff
fixes.whatChanges: In 2019 Julian Richer put 60% of Richer Sounds, a UK entertainment retailer with 53 stores, into a trust for its employees, and each of 522 staff got £1,000 for every year they'd worked there, about £8,000 on average. Owners are often more open to this when they hear how another owner did it.
fixes.example: Richer Sounds employee ownership trust · United Kingdom · 2019 · Founder Julian Richer handed a 60% stake in the entertainment retailer, which has 53 stores across the UK, to a trust for staff; 522 employees got £1,000 per year of service, about £8,000 on average
fixes.firstStep: Send the story to one business owner you know who's thinking about stepping back.

item.title: Hospital bills cut or forgiven when I can’t pay
item.line: When a hospital bill comes, I find out whether I qualify to have it reduced or erased before I pay anything.

fixes.title: Ask the hospital for its financial assistance application
fixes.whatChanges: Nonprofit hospitals have to offer charity care that reduces or erases bills for patients under an income limit, and each hospital sets its own limit. Asking for the application is how you find out where you stand.
fixes.example: Dollar For charity care help · United States · 2019 · Free nonprofit that files hospital charity care applications; more than $38 million in medical bills cleared since 2019
fixes.firstStep: Search your hospital’s name with the words financial assistance policy, and download the application.

fixes.title: Let a free nonprofit file the application for you
fixes.whatChanges: Dollar For, a nonprofit, prepares charity care applications, sends them to the hospital and follows up, at no cost to patients. The group says it has helped clear more than $38 million in medical bills since 2019.
fixes.example: Dollar For charity care help · United States · 2019 · Free nonprofit that files hospital charity care applications; more than $38 million in medical bills cleared since 2019
fixes.firstStep: Answer the eligibility questions on Dollar For’s website with your household size and income.

fixes.title: Ask for an itemized bill before you pay
fixes.whatChanges: An itemized bill lists every charge, so you can spot duplicates or services you never received. Ask for it before you agree to a payment plan.
fixes.firstStep: Call the billing number on your statement and ask for an itemized bill with the billing codes.

item.painLine: I'm worried about the planet heating up.
item.title: Getting solar power without owning a roof
item.line: Part of the electricity I pay for comes from a solar farm nearby, and my bill is a little lower for it.

fixes.title: Subscribe to a community solar farm
fixes.whatChanges: In Minnesota, community solar gardens reached 939 megawatts in 2024, almost a third of the state’s solar, and subscribers’ bills are expected to drop 3% to 8%. Some people object that bills for non-subscribers rise 2% to 3%, which is why the program nearly ended in 2025.
fixes.example: Minnesota community solar garden program · Minnesota · 2025 · 939 MW in 2024, almost a third of the state's solar; subscribers' bills expected to fall 3% to 8%; repeal dropped in June 2025 after advocates rallied
fixes.firstStep: Search your state name with "community solar" and see whether any program serves your utility.

fixes.title: Ask your state lawmakers to allow plug-in solar panels
fixes.whatChanges: In 2025 Utah became the first state to let people plug solar systems of up to 1,200 watts straight into a home outlet, and the law passed with no votes against. The parts run a few hundred dollars, compared with a $30,000 rooftop quote, but no complete plug-in system had been certified by UL yet when Grist reported on the law.
fixes.example: Utah plug-in solar law (HB 340) · Utah · 2025 · Utah became the first state to allow residents to plug solar systems directly into home outlets; passed with no dissenting votes; output up to 1,200 watts; inverters about $300 and panels $250 to $1,000 versus a $30,000 rooftop quote; in Germany balcony panels added 10% more solar capacity
fixes.firstStep: Look up whether a plug-in solar bill has been filed in your state, and find the names of your two state lawmakers.

fixes.title: Find the community solar programs open to your address
fixes.whatChanges: Community solar rules differ by state and utility, and many people never hear about the programs they could join. It could check your utility and ZIP code and list the open programs, with what each would roughly save you.
fixes.firstStep: Tell us you'd use this, and find the name of your electric utility on your last bill.
